newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Newcrest to boost Telfer gold output.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Newcrest to boost Telfer gold output.

text.p: Newcrest Mining Ltd would increase production from its Telfer mine in Western Australia over the next two years to nearly 600,000 ounces of gold a year, managing director John Quinn told the annual meeting.
The mine produced 365,000 ounces in 1995/96.
Newcrest was pursuing initiatives to extend the life of Telfer, which would remain the company's core asset for the foreseeable future, Quinn said.
He said higher output would flow from expanded dump leach treatment at 24 million tonnes of ore a year and from increased underground output as deep discoveries were fully developed.

"There is no reason to believe that we will not be able to sustain these higher production levels for a significant period in light of Telfer's large resource and reserve base and its continuing exploration potential," Quinn said.

Latest deep drilling at Telfer's West Dome provided encouraging results, "the best deep intersection we have made to date at West Dome," he said. The best deep intersection was of three substantial zones of mineralisation.
The upper zone was 27.3 metres at 4.25 grams a tonne (g/t) gold from 1,051 metres. This included a higher grade zone of about five metres at 18.0 g/t gold.
The middle zone returned 16.9 metres at 3.05 g/t gold from 1,306 metres which included 3.6 metres at 7.6 g/t.
The lower zone returned 15.7 metres at 3.8 g/t gold from 1,410 metres.
Further assay results were awaited, but it was expected that each of the three zones would also contain a "meaningful copper result," he said.
Further drilling to determine significance would be undertaken without delay, he said.
Executive general manager development Courtney Chamberlain said drilling results received on Wednesday from the Cadia gold mine, 20 km south of Orange in New South Wales, were "very exciting".
"(They) clearly reinforce the magnitude, extent and as-yet untapped potential of this system," he said.
A 308 metre zone in the latest hole at Cadia East from 1,069 metres down graded 1.06 g/t gold and 0.44 percent copper.
Included in this intersectiopn was 159 metres grading 1.73 g/t gold and 0.50 percent copper. More results were awaited, he said.

Chamberlain described the A$441 million Cadia development as "very large-scale", with modest grades but with significant planned production of nearly 300,000 ounces of gold and 23,000 tonnes of copper a year.
This would provide a 50 percent boost to Newcrest's current total annual gold output. Costs of production were currently estimated at less than A$300 an ounce.
"We confidently expect the (Cadia mine) life will be considerably longer (than the current estimate of more than 12 years) when we are in a position to schedule in the East Cadia orebody," he said.
After a "flying start" at Cadia, Newcrest expected to ship its first concentrates to two Japanese smelters, under long-term contract arrangements already signed, in October 1998, he said.

The Gosowong gold prospect in eastern Indonesia, part of a concession which Newcrest is exploring in association with Indonesian state-owned PT Aneka Tambang, had provided "some spectacular grades", he said.
An investment of A$70 million to put Gosowong into production would produce a "very quick pay back", he said.
Newcrest expected to nearly double gold output to more than one million ounces a year with Cadia and Gosowong in production.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
